chunks: And Ḥammād narrated from Abū Ayyūb:
He asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who caught a fish, then tied it with a string and sent it back into the water, and it died. Is it eaten? He said: "No."

key_terms.أَ تُؤْكَلُ: is it permissible to eat it
key_terms.لَا: no; it is not to be eaten

ai.seo_question: Can a fish be eaten if it was caught, tied with a string, returned to the water, and then died?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the permissibility of eating a fish after it was caught, tied, returned to the water, and then died there. The Imam عليه السلام rules that such a fish is not to be eaten, indicating a jurisprudential condition relevant to lawful catch.
